mission.name: IDC Forge Cross-Harness Gauntlet
mission.tagline: One canonical forge, portable by proof rather than proclamation.
mission.northStar: Preserve the fifty-island source while every compatibility claim is falsifiable, tiered, and reproducible on the harness that consumes it.

policies.notes: Local branches and commits are permitted for isolation and recovery. No push, PR, release, or profile install without explicit user authority. The 400-line target is advisory for generated mission/report assets and test fixtures.

phases.title: Contract and red-capable tooling
phases.goal: Replace portability claims with a sourced harness contract, a repo-owned validator, and a Windows-native installer/exporter.

gates.title: Harness support matrix is valid JSON
gates.notes: Verified 15 harness surfaces and the idc.harness-support/v1.1 schema; the contract also received blind artifact critique.

gates.title: Validator and installer falsification tests pass
gates.notes: 41 tests executed on Windows: 40 passed and one POSIX-only case skipped; the same installer suite passed 24/24 under WSL during its repair lane.

gates.title: All canonical skills pass repo-owned validation
gates.notes: Canonical profile passed 50/50 with zero errors and thirteen named compatibility advisories.

tasks.notes: Builder A owns docs/harness-support.md and docs/harness-support.json in an isolated worktree.

tasks.title: Build dependency-free whole-forge validator

tasks.notes: Builder b1ab04c3 was blind-critiqued, repaired at 3ce33f49, and integrated; Windows and WSL suites cover transaction preflight, Unicode output, metadata collisions, and POSIX mode drift.

phases.title: Gauntlet critique and integration
phases.goal: Blind critics refute each artifact, builders repair surviving findings, and the integration branch receives only evidenced changes.

tasks.title: Integrate approved local commits and align canon/docs
tasks.notes: All repaired commits and critique records are integrated locally; no remote write occurred.

phases.title: Recursive fifty-island health sweep
phases.goal: Run the stricter contract over every island and keep only skill changes tied to concrete red cases.

gates.title: Canonical profile passes for all fifty islands
gates.notes: 50/50 canonical pass; all thirteen compatibility advisories remain named.

gates.title: Compatibility exports are deterministic and current claude.ai incompatibility fails closed
gates.notes: Historical supplied profile produced and verified 50 deterministic root-folder ZIPs; current profile created no output and named 48 description plus 13 invocation blockers.

tasks.notes: All fifty skills were swept; canonical failures were zero and every compatibility advisory is enumerated by skill and invariant.

tasks.title: Repair only evidenced canonical defects
tasks.notes: No island workflow was rewritten: the canonical profile exposed no workflow defect. Only the authoring canon's false distribution claim was corrected and revalidated.

tasks.title: Update authoring and install documentation to the proved support matrix
tasks.notes: README, registry, and idc-skill-authoring now route portability claims through the versioned support contract and fail-closed exporter.

risks.title: No different-family reviewer is callable from this Codex session
risks.note: The three critiques are blind and non-author, but cross-family-review was unavailable and no output is labeled a cross-family verdict.

risks.title: Several requested harnesses may not expose a native Agent Skills loader
risks.note: Buzz and Grok Bot remain unsupported/unknown, native-Windows Hermes has a failed observation, and several authenticated behavior probes remain partial or unrun. The matrix does not invent installation paths.

risks.title: The complete current pack is intentionally blocked from claude.ai export
risks.note: Current public documentation imposes a 200-character description limit and does not establish an explicit-only equivalent for thirteen user-invoked islands. No live upload or routing probe was run.

risks.title: Whole-run rollback stops at the unexpected-I/O boundary
risks.note: Every destination is preflighted and each skill replacement is atomic, but a multi-skill or multi-target run is not rollback-atomic after an unexpected mid-run I/O failure.

nextActions: If publication is desired, review local branch codex/gauntlet-integration and explicitly authorize a push or pull request.
Run authenticated loader and invocation probes for the matrix entries still marked partial, unrun, failed, or unsupported.
Treat claude.ai description shortening as a separate skill-tune experiment: preserve routing on representative tasks before accepting any <=200-character rewrite.
blockers: Universal runtime portability is not proved: Buzz and Grok Bot remain unsupported/unknown, and native-Windows Hermes did not load the sampled Forge islands.
Current claude.ai export remains blocked by 48 over-limit descriptions and 13 user-only invocation semantics; a live upload was not run.
Cross-family verdict unavailable: this session could spawn only OpenAI-family sub-agents.
Remote publication remains outside current authority; all branches and commits are local.
conventions: ops/mission/state.json is the source of truth; never hand-edit state-of-the-union.html.
Positive harness claims require an authoritative source and reproducible probe.
Canonical skill bytes are preserved unless a red-capable evaluation justifies an edit.
Worktree evidence is draft evidence until re-derived from a fresh clone.
A historical compatibility transform preserves metadata values only; it never asserts invocation semantics.
